newsitem.title: INDIA: India Indo Rama to set up $100 mln unit.
newsitem.headline: India Indo Rama to set up $100 mln unit.

text.p: Indo Rama Synthetics (India) Ltd, one of India's largest private polyester producers, said on Friday it expected a new spinning and weaving unit at Karnataka to become operational by mid-1998.
The company said in a statement that the $100 million plant, to be located at Dharwad in India's southern state of Karnataka, would have a capacity of 30 million metres annually.
"The setting up of this unit is in line with the company's strategy of expansion of its operations," the statement quoted Indo Rama Managing Director O.P. Lohia as saying.
The integration is expected to reduce Indo Rama's dependence on external factors and strengthen the consistency of its products, the statement said.
The Dharwad facility will have a spinning capacity of 50,000 spindles and 240 looms for weaving, it added.
Polyester Staple Fibre (PSF) is to be sourced from the company's Butibori plant while cotton for its spinning operations is to be sourced locally.
"The new plant is expected to further establish Indo Rama's leadership position in productivity and lower production cost," the statement said.
Indo Rama Synthetics (India) Ltd is part of the $800 million Indo Rama group which has operations in Indonesia, Thailand, Nepal and Sri Lanka, the statement said.
It has an installed capacity of 122,880 spindles for blended yarn and 250,000 tonnes annually of PSF and POY (Partially-Oriented Yarn) in India.
The statement added that the firm set up operations in India in 1989 and has since grown to be the country's second largest polyester producer, with a market share of 22 percent.
